newsitem.title: FRANCE: BNP regrets CIC privatisation halt.
newsitem.headline: BNP regrets CIC privatisation halt.

text.p: French bank BNP said on Thursday it regretted the government's decision to call off the sale of CIC bank, for which BNP had made an offer.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said earlier on Thursday that the privatisation procedure had been halted.

Arthuis said the privatisation commission had decided that a BNP offer complied with the sell-off conditions but an offer by Societe Generale had been rejected by the commission and that the sale procedure was therefore being halted.
A BNP spokeswoman, contacted by Reuters, declined to say if the bank would make a fresh offer if there was a new tender.
"BNP notes with regret the Finance Minister's decision to break off the CIC privatisation procedure," a BNP statement said.

The bank said it welcomed the fact that its offer had been the only one accepted by the French privatisation commission as complying with all the terms and conditions which the government had attached to the sell-off, especially on preserving CIC's regional integrity.

"This confirms that the criticisms levelled at BNP in the past weeks were totally unfounded," it said, noting that it had been unable to explain its offer during the course of the sale tender due to a confidentiality clause.

A CIC spokeswoman said in response to a query from Reuters that the bank had no immediate comment on the cancellation of the sell-off process or on comments by Arthuis that CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt had not helped to promote the privatisation.
